summary.text: Jeffrey Dinowitz is the incumbent Democratic Assembly Member for District 81 in the Bronx, first elected in 1994. Before the Assembly he was a New York State administrative law judge and a longtime local party official. He chairs the Assembly's Codes Committee, has previously chaired several other committees, and his official biography lists a range of enacted laws he authored.

paragraphs.text: Dinowitz was born in 1954 and has lived in the Bronx all his life. He is a graduate of Bronx public schools, the Bronx High School of Science, Herbert H. Lehman College (CUNY), and Brooklyn Law School; Ballotpedia lists a bachelor's degree from Lehman in 1975 and a law degree from Brooklyn Law School in 1979.

Before his election to the Assembly he served as an Administrative Law Judge for the State of New York. Ballotpedia also lists professional experience at the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles, as an attorney in the New York City Comptroller's office, and as an assistant counsel for the New York State Assembly.

His party roles include election as a State Committeeman in 1978 and service as a District Leader from 1986 to 1994; his official biography says he led a team of reformers into party office in 1986. He was a delegate to his party's national convention in 1980, 1996, 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, and 2020, chaired its Bronx County Committee from 2008 to 2016, and has been its Secretary from 2018 to the present.
He was elected to the Assembly to represent the 81st District on February 15, 1994.

He chairs the Assembly Committee on Codes and serves on the Rules, Ways and Means, Health, and Election Law committees. He previously chaired the Judiciary, Corporations/Authorities and Commissions, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Aging, and Alcoholism and Drug Abuse committees.

He has authored numerous enacted laws, including the Anti-Human Trafficking Act (2007), the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (2014), the MTA Lockbox law (2018), the repeal of the non-medical vaccine exemption for schoolchildren (2019), and the COVID-19 Emergency Eviction and Foreclosure Prevention Act (2020/21).

His official biography cites his local work as leading opposition to the Bronx water filtration plant, helping spearhead a business improvement district in Kingsbridge, and being a major force in creating two new middle/high schools in Riverdale and Kingsbridge.
According to his official biography, he has been married to Sylvia Gottlieb since 1978 and they have two children and four grandchildren.
